brief: Weekly GS Sales/Trading positioning snapshot for the week of 5 Oct. Fundamental long/short funds derisked for a third straight week, net leverage at its lowest since Apr '25 and near five-year (2nd percentile) lows. The non-fundamental bid is weakening: CTAs are forecast to sell $18.5bn of global equities this week, trend signals sit near threshold levels that could trigger larger unwinds, and the corporate buyback bid looks constrained by the pre-earnings blackout (93% of S&P 500 in blackout, rising to 94%). Europe is framed as a relative hideout: PB clients showed risk-on flows for a second straight week (new longs outpacing short covers) and EPFR recorded inflows to Western Europe equity funds, while North America funds kept seeing outflows. Prime-brokerage books overall were net bought (+0.7 SDs), led by long buys over short sales (2.7:1), though single stocks were net sold for a third week. Retail stayed a sustained buyer and AAII/GS/CNN sentiment gauges remain depressed. The desk's conclusion: depressed sentiment plus cautious fundamental positioning offers contrarian support heading into Q4.
